issues.description: It is not obvious which 3MF mode fits 'both parts in one 3MF, printed in one go'. 'objects' (the default) gives two objects, and 'multimaterial' gives one object with material regions. I used the default.
I found no way to set the 3MF mode in cad.toml [export]. It is only a CLI flag.
I found no direct check that the two parts touch without overlapping. cad clearance only covers reference parts. I relied on the bboxes, the volumes and the section render.

The task says 'one 3MF with both parts' but it is not obvious whether to use objects mode (default) or multimaterial mode. I chose the default (two objects, each with its own material). The docs do not say which one a slicer user should pick for a recess plus insert.
cad.toml [export] has no documented key for the 3MF mode. A later 'cad export --format 3mf' without the flag silently overwrote the multimaterial file with an objects-mode file.
Section render paints every cut face the same red, so the PLA/TPU boundary is only a thin line and the two materials can't be told apart in the cut.

The docs don't say which 3MF mode fits 'one file, both parts, one print'. I used the default (objects: one object per part). I didn't exercise multimaterial mode, and cad.toml has no documented key for it.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a per-project 3mf_mode option in cad.toml.
Add a 'cad measure --contact' or an overlap/contact report between parts.
Print the 3MF overlap-check result in the export output even when it passes.
Add a recipe for 'recess plus insert': cut the recess in one part and add a matching cylinder as a second part.
Have cad inspect or cad clearance report contact and overlap between parts, to confirm that the parts touch without overlapping.
Colour section cut faces by part material.
Document a cad.toml [export] key for the 3MF mode.
Add a cad measure/query that reports touching or overlapping parts and their contact area, so flush-fit insets can be checked numerically.
